Beta Readerگزارش فارسی

Annotation Questions and Review

114 surahs examined; 82 reference pages protected; 788 quotation spans and 1129 underline changes in 32 targets.

This is an editorial beta, not a certified interpretation. 173 items need an annotation decision; 215 are pending coverage checks, not demonstrated ambiguities; 2 are mechanical source checks. All three are kept distinct. Reference pages remain unchanged.

Interpretation Rules

  • Solid = good. Dotted = bad. Dashed = neither good nor bad. Judge the actual phrase's function in context; a neutral object remains distinct from the good or bad act around it.
  • Gray level separates groups, not meanings. Nearby independent groups use different gray levels; a group's own members retain a consistent level.
  • Green and red are reserved for a nearby good/bad comparison. The green good alternative stays solid; the red bad alternative is dotted. Color does not override the pattern rule. Unpaired comparison colors were changed to gray in the reviewed targets.
  • Quotation colors distinguish speakers locally and are independent of underline polarity. A speaker's identity does not make every word in the quote good or bad.
  • Opening signs are placed before the first quoted word on the right, and closing signs after the last quoted word on the left, with explicit RTL isolation. Closing markers no longer spill into the next paragraph or its bullet.
  • Do not close quotes at every verse. Keep multi-verse speech and embedded reports separate; do not include narrator commentary or mistake a reporting instruction for an actual utterance.
  • All Quranic wording and whitespace, vertical-line markup, and 82 reference HTML files are preserved. The clarified semantic convention is applied to target annotations; protected reference exceptions are not silently rewritten.

This semantic pass reviews 190 good, 196 bad, and 86 neutral existing underline changes, plus 615 new underline spans. 110 local red/green groups are saved in advance. These checks do not certify every unreviewed phrase or every legacy group assignment.

Audit files: applied changes, explicit semantic roles, boundary refinements, reference evidence, review items.

Corrections From This Review

4:118-119 — reviewed quotation correction
Previously
The red quotation began at ولأضلنهم in verse 119, omitting the same speaker's preceding vow.
Corrected
Begin at لأتخذن من عبادك in verse 118 and continue through the vow in verse 119; stop before ومن يتخذ, where the warning/commentary begins.
Reason
The explicit وقال in verse 118 introduces the same uninterrupted first-person speech continued by coordinated verbs in verse 119.
6:50 — reviewed quotation correction
Previously
Only the first response introduced by قل had quotation signs.
Corrected
Add a separate black pair for هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير through the verse ending, following the second قل.
Reason
A second reporting command starts a separate response; it is not part of the preceding response's narration.
6:56 — reviewed quotation correction
Previously
Only the first response introduced by قل had quotation signs.
Corrected
Add a separate black pair for لا أتبع أهواءكم through the verse ending, following the second قل.
Reason
The second explicit reporting command was previously left without its own paired markers.
  • Continuous quotations now include their earlier starts in 5:27-29 and 6:78-79; Abraham's speech continues through 21:57.
  • The opposing reply in 5:27 and the reply in 26:74 now have separate paired signs.
  • The unsupported direct-utterance layer around the reporting instruction in 17:53 was removed and left in the review queue.
  • Closing markers are anchored to the last quoted text, outside its final inline underline, not to the start of the next paragraph.
  • The earlier false uncertainty flags for wavy underlines and symbol markers remain removed.

Passage-by-Passage Underline Review

783 explicitly reviewed phrases in 377 passage groups across all 32 target surahs. The beta now has 615 newly added spans and 514 existing underline edits, including spacing repairs. Exact existing phrases are reviewed in place; missing subphrases can be nested; inline-markup crossings no longer silently block application.

A good prohibition can contain a dotted bad object, and an approved action can contain a dashed neutral object. These remain different semantic layers with separate visible line levels. The table records the actual planned phrases and reasons; it does not claim that every remaining phrase in all 114 surahs has been certified.

Latest Scope and Saved-Group Audit

  • The short answer الله in 6:91 now opens only after its explicitly reviewed قل cue, not at an earlier occurrence of the same word. All repeated starts require an explicit cue or occurrence.
  • The construction account in 18:95-96 separates the instructions from the narrated levelling/heating and the two later قال turns.
  • The disputant's account in 38:23 has its own layer and a nested pair around the alleged demand أكفلنيها; the following account of pressure is outside that inner pair.
  • All 117 pages require a persisted group index. 8307 underline IDs and 4391 groups were checked against HTML and JSON. The viewer loads those saved arrays directly and has no inference fallback when a page opens.

The internal-reporting-cue audit is a diagnostic aid, not a proof of semantic correctness. Remaining interpretive questions below stay open. Saved-group and scope audit.

All-Target Underline Inventory

The scan examined 3415 indexed source verses in all 32 targets. 303 verses have explicit passage decisions. 1634 still have unreviewed structural cues. These are possible omissions, not proven mistakes or assigned semantic groups. A lack of a simple cue also does not certify a verse.

The complete table prevents an unreviewed passage from disappearing from the report. Span detection here is lexical/coarse; it is not a semantic coverage score. The source's verse labels are retained, including the separately reported numbering issue.
